messages:
david: Heads-up — I put together a sketch for a more conservative autoscaler for spot-backed inference pools. We've been hitting spikes where the fast scale-out floods AZs with preemptibles and then we get a cascade of evictions + prolonged cooldowns. Thinking we need per-az backpressure + an eviction-aware cooldown multiplier.
sarah: nice — can you summarize the high-level levers you want?
david: sure. Short list: 1) dual triggers: demand (queue length / p50 qps) and eviction signal (recent preemption rate). 2) dynamic cooldown multiplier when eviction_rate > threshold. 3) a small hard reserve (min_headroom GPUs) per-AZ that we only top up with on-demand or reserved when eviction gating trips. 4) max_surge as a pct of fleet not absolute instances.
kevin: +1. we should also gate scale-outs based on network egress capacity per-AZ — last time we brought 40% extra nodes and saturated the AZ fabric. could be a separate gating metric.
iulia: question — how do we avoid oscillation between on-demand and spot when the reserve kicks in? we don't want churn moving work back and forth.
david: good point. plan is: when reserve is used we flip to a slow reconciliation mode (longer evaluation window, exponential cooldown) and mark affected allocations sticky for N minutes so placement doesn't shift unless real demand changes.
infra-bot: NOTE: cluster-autoscaler vX.9 deployed to canary yesterday. It supports custom gating hooks via /autoscale/gates.
sarah: can you paste the proposed config snippet? makes it easier to review.
david: pasting a minimal example (pseudo-yaml):
```
autoscaler:
  triggers:
    - type: queue_length
      scale_out_threshold: 1200  # total requests in 30s
      window: 30s
    - type: eviction_rate
      window: 5m
      threshold: 0.025  # 2.5% recent evictions
  headroom:
    min_headroom_gpus_per_az: 1
    reserved_on_demand_policy: prefer_reserved_if_eviction
  surge_control:
    max_surge_fraction: 0.12  # 12% of current fleet size
    max_surge_absolute: 30
  cooldown:
    base_seconds: 45
    multiplier_on_eviction: 4  # cooldown = base * multiplier
  backpressure:
    network_egress_threshold_mbps_per_az: 6000
```
kevin: I like the network gate. Also suggest adding "model-hotness" weighting — small models that ramp qps shouldn't trigger as aggressively as long-running chat sessions.
iulia: ACK on sticky allocation. we should also prefer heterogeneous gpu mix during surge: i.e., prefer cheaper mips if latency budget allows. suggestion: scale_out_target_mix: [p4:0.4, g5:0.6]
david: yup — propose mixing via model profiles. we do model->latency_budget check before selecting flavor. if a model is latency-sensitive, it pins to faster HW and counts against surge budget separately.
sarah: any metrics we should start collecting now to validate?
david: collect: per-az eviction_rate (1m/5m), per-az network_utilization, preemptible_start_rate (how many new spot instances started per minute), per-model queue_length pctiles, churn (nodes moved between ondemand/spot). Also add an experiment tag when reserve is used.
kevin: ops note — if cooldown_multiplier_on_eviction is too high we might not recover capacity fast enough during true demand spikes. maybe cap multiplier to 3 and add a fast-path: if queue_length > 3x threshold AND eviction_rate falling, allow an emergency override (but limited).
infra-bot: ACTION: created /autoscale/experiments/spot-backpressure-2026 with canary scope = us-west-2c. Deployed config revision 19 to canary.
iulia: timeline?
david: canary for 24h, collect metrics, then roll to 20% of fleet for 6h if stable.
sarah: one more thing — cost target: keep overall spot usage >= 70% but allow temporary increase in on-demand to satisfy headroom. add a rolling cost check so we don't bleed budget.
kevin: adding a guard: if cost_spike_pct > 20% over baseline for last 1h, disable reserve->on-demand conversions automatically and alert finance.
iulia: test plan: synthetic QPS ramp, then inject simulated evictions (via fault-injector) and watch for: no AZ saturation, capped surge, cooldown behavior, and sticky allocations hold.
david: sounds good. I'll open a PR with the autoscaler hook + config and a runbook for the canary. tagging @kevin @sarah for review. :thumbsup:
sarah: thanks — will review PR this afternoon.
kevin: ack, will run the synthetic tests in staging tomorrow.
infra-bot: DEPLOY: autoscaler-rev19 applied to canary (us-west-2c) at 2151234600
kevin: seeing initial metrics — eviction_rate spiked to 0.04 for 30s during test, autoscaler applied multiplier (x4) and limited surge to 10% as configured. logs: 
```
[2151234610] scale_out_requested: +24 gpus (mix g5:0.6, p4:0.4)
[2151234612] surge_limit_reached: capped at 10%
[2151234620] cooldown: base=45s multiplier=4 => cooldown=180s
[2151234635] reserve_on_demand_allocated: 2 instances
```
kevin: preliminary: no network saturation observed, eviction_rate fell back to 0.01 after 2m.
iulia: great — let's let canary run the 24h and reconvene tomorrow to decide 20% rollout.
david: perfect. thanks everyone.
